items.heading: Somewhere Along the Way, "Average
items.text: Somewhere Along the Way, "Average Somewhere Along the Way, "Average Somewhere along the way, "average marks" quietly turned into "average person" in a lot of Indian households. That jump is not supported by anything real - it survives because school systems are built around one narrow test, and that test gets treated as a stand-in for a much bigger question it was never designed to answer.

items.heading: Chasing a "Backup" Degree Chasing
items.text: Chasing a "Backup" Degree Chasing a "backup" degree with no skill plan attached. A generic BA or BCom taken only because "some degree is needed" rarely opens doors by itself. The degree without a built skill on top of it is what actually stalls people - not the degree, and not the marks that got them into it.

items.heading: Instead of One Generic "Options
items.text: Instead of one generic "options for low scorers" list, it is more useful to think in lanes - broad categories of work that genuinely do not step entry on your board percentage. They are ordered below by real growth headroom rather than by which one sounds safest: business and freelance work leads because it is the only lane where you set your own pricing and can eventually hire or systemise the work, skill-first tech follows for its fast-growing, portfolio-driven demand, and government and defence roles close the list last - genuinely low on marks pressure, but capped by a fixed pay scale rather than open-ended growth. Each lane below has its own real trade-offs, and none of them require you to have topped anything.

Whether you can hold a long, demanding job well
Career success research points to problem-solving, resilience, communication, and initiative as the real predictors - none of which a board exam measures.
Whether recruiters will hire you at all
80% of Indian employers now say they would rather hire proven skill over a better degree, up from under 40% in 2020 - the fastest hiring shift in a decade.

items.heading: Treating One Exam Season As
items.text: Treating one exam season as a permanent verdict. A 3-hour paper on one day measures recall under pressure, not your ability to think, build, sell, lead, or fix things. Career-outcome research consistently finds problem-solving, resilience, and initiative are the real predictors of long-term success - traits no board exam scores.

items.heading: Ruling Out Government Exams Without
items.text: Ruling out government exams without checking the real eligibility line. Most students assume competitive government exams need board toppers. SSC CGL needs a plain pass certificate for most posts. Checking the actual cutoff takes ten minutes and often removes a wrongly-assumed barrier.

items.heading: Waiting to "Feel Ready" Before
items.text: Waiting to "feel ready" before building any proof of work. A finished small project - one deployed page, one client task done well, one documented repair job - beats another year of waiting to feel confident enough to start.

items.heading: IT Jumps Straight
items.text: It jumps straight to a short consolation list - "try BA, try a diploma" - without checking whether stronger doors are actually open.

items.heading: IT Rarely Separates What Marks
items.text: It rarely separates what marks genuinely affect (admission cutoffs, some scholarships) from what they do not (whether you can build a strong career).
